questions.q: What state are analytics.dim_product, dim_customer, dim_date, and fact_orders in right after Lesson 4's CREATE TABLE statements run?
options: Empty — CREATE TABLE only defines shape, it doesn't load any rows
Already fully loaded with every order
Partially loaded with last month's data
Deleted automatically after creation
questions.explain: CREATE TABLE defines structure only. Nothing is loaded until a COPY (or similar load) runs.

questions.q: Why is row-by-row INSERT the wrong tool for loading the curated dataset into fact_orders?
options: INSERT doesn't support the order_total column
It's a single serial operation with no parallelism, and it ignores the Parquet files already sitting in the curated zone
Redshift doesn't support INSERT at all
INSERT only works with CSV files, never with structured data
questions.explain: A single-row INSERT runs serially through the leader node and discards the bulk, columnar shape the ETL job already wrote.

questions.q: In the COPY statement, what does FORMAT AS PARQUET let Redshift do?
options: Convert the table to Parquet storage internally
Skip the IAM_ROLE clause entirely
Read the source files' embedded schema directly instead of guessing types from text
Compress the target table after loading
questions.explain: Parquet carries its own schema, so COPY can read column types directly rather than inferring them from delimited text.

questions.q: What is the IAM_ROLE clause in the COPY statement actually doing?
options: Telling Redshift which IAM role to assume so it can read the S3 source location on your behalf
Encrypting the connection between Redshift and the client
Creating a new IAM user for the load
Granting the role permission to delete the source files after loading
questions.explain: S3 buckets have no username/password login; COPY assumes an IAM role whose policy grants it read access to the source.

questions.q: What does a COPY statement returning without an error actually confirm?
options: Only that the statement ran to completion — not that the loaded data is complete or correct
That the data is guaranteed correct and complete
That the source S3 files have been deleted
That the Glue ETL job has also finished running
questions.explain: A clean return means the load ran without erroring; actually confirming completeness and correctness is a separate validation step, covered in Lesson 6.
